paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is not hard to reach, even when He's trying to lie low. He goes into one house in the region of Tyre, not wanting anyone to know He's there, and a mom with a sick little girl still finds Him (Mark 7:24-25). She is a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she keeps asking (Mark 7:26). Then she gets a picture about the children's bread, and she answers with "Yes, Lord," and holds on (Mark 7:27-28).

Look at what Jesus says to her: "Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter" (Mark 7:29). She didn't have the perfect words, she had a humble, hanging-on kind of faith, and she got her little girl back (Mark 7:30). I have shown up to the oven with a half-baked plan more times than I can count, so this one encourages me, friend. Keep coming to Jesus, keep asking, and keep trusting Him when the answer doesn't look like what you expected.

Then we meet a deaf man whose friends bring him to Jesus and beg for Him to place His hand on him (Mark 7:32). Jesus takes him aside, speaks "Ephphatha!" which means "Be opened!", and immediately the man hears and speaks plainly (Mark 7:33-35). Jesus told them not to tell anyone, but the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it, and the people said, "He has done all things well!" (Mark 7:36-37). So here's your takeaway, baker: bring your people to Jesus, bring yourself too, and then go ahead and tell it, because everything He does, He does well.
